cues.en: Something else. So they were very skillful. Yeah. But
cues.zh: 另外，他们确实很有本事。是啊，不过

cues.en: they did show us. Yeah. So,
cues.zh: 他们确实给我们看了。是啊，所以，

cues.en: and it's good that they showed us because the technology crashed and burned at Xerox.
cues.zh: 他们给我们看是件好事，因为这项技术在施乐公司彻底失败了。

cues.en: They used to call the- What's that? No, I was just- Why? Yeah, why? Oh, very, I actually thought a lot about that. And I learned more about that with John Scully later on, and I think I understand it now pretty well. What happens is,
cues.zh: 他们以前把……那是什么？不，我刚才只是……为什么？对，为什么？哦，这个嘛，我确实想过很多。后来我和约翰·斯卡利聊了之后，对这件事了解得更多了。我想我现在已经相当明白了。情况是这样的，

cues.en: like with John Scully,
cues.zh: 比如约翰·斯卡利，

cues.en: John came from PepsiCo.
cues.zh: 约翰之前在百事公司工作。

cues.en: And they at most would change their product, you know, once every ten years. I mean to them a new product was like a new size bottle, right? So if you were a product person,
cues.zh: 他们顶多每十年才更新一次产品，对他们来说，所谓新产品无非就是换个新尺寸的瓶子，对吧？所以如果你是个做产品的人，

cues.en: you couldn't change the course of that company very much. So who influenced the success of PepsiCo? The sales and marketing people. Therefore, they were the ones that got promoted and therefore they were the ones that ran the company.
cues.zh: 你根本无法左右这家公司的走向。那么是谁在决定百事公司的成功？是销售和市场人员。因此，得到晋升的是他们，最终掌管公司的也是他们。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: for PepsiCo that might have been okay,
cues.zh: 对百事可乐来说，那可能没什么问题，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但

cues.en: it turns out the same thing can happen in technology companies that get monopolies,
cues.zh: 事实证明，同样的事情也会发生在获得垄断地位的科技公司身上，

cues.en: like, oh, IBM and Xerox.
cues.zh: 比如 IBM 和施乐。

cues.en: If you were a product person at IBM or Xerox,
cues.zh: 如果你是 IBM 或施乐的产品人员，

cues.en: so you make a better copy or a better computer. So what? When you have a monopoly market share, the company's not any more successful.
cues.zh: 你做出了更好的复印机或更好的电脑，那又怎样？当公司拥有垄断性市场份额时，公司也不会因此更成功。

cues.en: So the people that can make the company more successful are sales and marketing people,
cues.zh: 所以能让公司更成功的人是销售和营销人员，

cues.en: and they end up running the companies.
cues.zh: 最终是他们掌管了公司。

cues.en: And the product people get driven out of the decision making forums.
cues.zh: 产品人员逐渐被排除在决策圈之外。

cues.en: And the companies forget
cues.zh: 公司也会忘记

cues.en: what it means to make great products.
cues.zh: 如何打造出色的产品。

cues.en: It sort of the product
cues.zh: 产品方面的

cues.en: sensibility
cues.zh: 判断力，

cues.en: and the product genius that brought them to that monopolistic position gets rotted out
cues.zh: 以及当初让公司取得垄断地位的产品天赋，都会逐渐被消磨殆尽。

cues.en: by people running these companies who have no conception
cues.zh: 因为经营这些公司的人根本不懂

cues.en: of a good product versus a bad product. They have no conception of the craftsmanship that's required to take a good idea and turn it into a good product. And they really have no feeling in their hearts, usually,
cues.zh: 什么是好产品，什么是坏产品。他们不懂把一个好点子变成好产品需要怎样的匠心。通常，他们心里也根本没有那份真心，

cues.en: about wanting to really help the customers.
cues.zh: 想要真正帮助客户。

cues.en: So that's what happened at Xerox. The people at Xerox PARK used to call the people that ran Xerox toner heads.
cues.zh: 这就是当年在 Xerox 发生的事。Xerox PARC 的人过去把管理 Xerox 的高层叫做“碳粉脑壳”。

cues.en: And they just had, these toner heads would come out to Xerox PARK and they just had no clue about what they were seeing. And for our audience, toner is what? Oh, toner. Toner is what you put into a copier.
cues.zh: 这些“碳粉脑壳”来到 Xerox PARC，完全看不懂眼前看到的一切。给观众解释一下，toner 是什么？哦，碳粉，就是加进复印机里的那种。

cues.en: Yeah, you know, the toner that you add to an industrial copier? The black stuff. The black stuff, yeah. So
cues.zh: 对，就是加进工业复印机里的碳粉。黑乎乎的那种。对，黑色的粉末。所以

cues.en: basically they were copier heads that just had no clue about
cues.zh: 他们本质上就是一群复印机脑袋，对计算机完全一窍不通，

cues.en: a computer or what it could do. And so they just
cues.zh: 根本不知道它能干什么。于是他们硬是把

cues.en: grabbed defeat from the greatest victory in the computer industry.
cues.zh: 计算机工业史上最伟大的胜利，生生搞成了惨败。

cues.en: Xerox could have owned the entire computer industry today.
cues.zh: 施乐本可以拥有今天的整个计算机产业。

cues.en: Could have been, you know, a company 10 times its size. Could have been IBM.
cues.zh: 本可以成为规模十倍于此的公司。本可以成为IBM。

cues.en: Could have been the IBM of the nineties. Could have been the Microsoft of the nineties.
cues.zh: 本可以成为九十年代的IBM。本可以成为九十年代的微软。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: but anyway, that's all ancient history. It doesn't really matter anymore. Sure.
cues.zh: 但不管怎样，那都是陈年旧事了。现在已经无所谓了。当然。
